sourceChain.fact: Existing catch-all maps thrown session/context/DB errors to HTTP403.
Context/database/device-session reads can throw to the route.
403 is workspace refusal; it invalidates the provider. Plain500 does not.
Invalidation increments provider generation and router.refresh; children remount.

environmentIncident.baselineComparison: route, workspace-switcher, persistent-cache and AuthenticatedReadCache unchanged from f3ef8f4a to local integration5a.
environmentIncident.conclusion: Server switcher403 and connection termination occurred in the same window. Source confirms an existing catch-all incorrectly classifies unknown backend/DB exceptions as403, which can retire the cache subtree. This is a confirmed actionable follow-up defect, not resolved by the candidate. The exact thrown error and remount instant were not captured; plain500 and an ordinary Retry do not by themselves imply this invalidation.

documentRequests.interpretation: No extra document request during the observed ordinary paths. Explicit Refresh and real workspace assign/redirect are counted separately; this does not mean all React subtrees stayed mounted.

visualAndOperatorLimitations: Global connection toast obscured local Retry or a composer corner in some full-width error screenshots. Only final narrow-thread screenshot supports the stated no-obstruction observation.
Failed helper locators and pointer actions blocked by a toast are operator/observation failures; they are not silently counted as product passes.
The group-pending screenshot does not show the failed item below the viewport; the later recovered screenshot and selected DOM evidence do.
No production shared-account, live model/tool, cross-account, multi-tab, or native-mobile acceptance claim.
